newsitem.title: POLAND: Warning strike expected at Polish Gdansk refinery.
newsitem.headline: Warning strike expected at Polish Gdansk refinery.

text.p: Workers of Poland's second largest refinery, Rafineria Gdanska SA, will hold a one-hour warning strike on February 5 to press for shares in the company and a pay rise, a union official said on Monday.

Andrzej Cenacewicz, the head of the Solidarity trade union in the refinery, told Reuters the action would be staged between 10 and 11 a.m. local time (0900-1000 GMT) and that production would not be halted.
"We haven't decided yet what would be the form of the protest. We might block the entrance but we certainly will not halt the production facilities," Cenacewicz said.
Four trade unions active in the refinery want workers to receive 15 percent of shares in the company for free, as envisaged by a privatisation bill passed last year.
They also demand a 17-percent pay rise in 1997 and a back pay increase for last year.
Cenacewicz said the decision about the warning strike was made after a referendum last week showed a majority of workers supported strike action to press their demands.
He said that on February 5 the unions are scheduled to begin talks with the management about their demands.

The refinery is 75-percent owned by the state oil holding Nafta Polska SA with the remaining 25 percent directly controlled by the state treasury. It processes about three million tonnes of crude oil annually.

The refinery's spokeswoman said earlier the management was ready to discuss pay issues with workers. But the management said the issue of free shares would have to wait until April 8, when a relevant privatisation law comes into force.
